questions.question_text: Tricyclic antidepressants:

options.text: Are slowly absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract because they are not lipid soluble
Have low protein binding
Are subject to a low first-pass metabolism
Have a plasma level linearly related to the clinical response
Are metabolized in the liver and metabolites are predominantly excreted by the kidney

correct_answer.text: Are metabolized in the liver and metabolites are predominantly excreted by the kidney

correct_answers.text: Are metabolized in the liver and metabolites are predominantly excreted by the kidney

questions.explanation: Tricyclic antidepressants have rapid absorption, are highly lipophilic and have high protein binding.

questions.question_text: Tricyclic antidepressants:

options.text: Commonly cause bradycardia and hypertension
Frequently cause prolongation of PR and QT intervals on ECG
Increase seizure threshold
Increase the plasma concentration of carbamazepine
When taken with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) increase MAOI-induced insomnia

correct_answer.text: Frequently cause prolongation of PR and QT intervals on ECG

correct_answers.text: Frequently cause prolongation of PR and QT intervals on ECG

questions.explanation: T ricyclic antidepressants commonly cause tachycardia and hypotension, and decrease seizure threshold and the plasma concentration of carbamazepine. When taken with MAOIs, they decrease MAOI-induced insomnia, and increase postural hypotension and weight gain.

questions.question_text: Phenelzine has significant interaction with all of the following, except:

options.text: Pethidine
Methylphenidate
Salbutamol
Metformin
ACE inhibitors

questions.explanation: Pethidine is used for CNS excitation or depression and may cause impaired consciousness and coma; methylphenidate is used for hypertensive crisis; metformin is used for hypoglycaemia; ACE inhibitors are used for enhanced hypotensive effect.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about serotonin syndrome, except:

options.text: It may occur with a combination of tranylcypromine and L-tryptophan
It is associated with myoclonus
It can be associated with hypomania
It can be fatal
The treatment of choice is sodium dantrolene

correct_answer.text: The treatment of choice is sodium dantrolene

correct_answers.text: The treatment of choice is sodium dantrolene

questions.explanation: Sodium dantrolene is used in patients with neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) and malignant hyperthermia. In 5-HT syndrome, treatment is mainly supportive and all medications should be stopped.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: First-pass metabolism could be avoided by sublingual administration of a drug
Highly protein-bound drugs are more likely to be secreted in the breast milk
Highly lipid-soluble drugs are more likely to be secreted in the breast milk
Highly water-soluble and ionized drugs cannot cross the blood–brain barrier easily
At steady state, the rate of removal of the drug equals the rate of input

correct_answer.text: Highly protein-bound drugs are more likely to be secreted in the breast milk

correct_answers.text: Highly protein-bound drugs are more likely to be secreted in the breast milk

questions.explanation: Protein binding can influence the drug's biological half-life in the body.

questions.question_text: Regarding pharmacokinetics:

options.text: A very high value of volume of distribution indicates that the drug is concentrated in the blood itself
The steady state of a drug is usually reached in 4–5 half-lives in first-order kinetics
Elimination of most drugs follows zero-order kinetics
Alcohol and phenytoin follow first-order kinetics
Tachyphylaxis is usually due to up-regulation or down-regulation of receptors

correct_answer.text: The steady state of a drug is usually reached in 4–5 half-lives in first-order kinetics

correct_answers.text: The steady state of a drug is usually reached in 4–5 half-lives in first-order kinetics

questions.explanation: A low volume of distribution indicates that the drug is concentrated in the blood itself; elimination of most drugs follows first-order kinetics, but alcohol and phenytoin follow zero-order kinetics. Tachyphylaxis is the very rapid development of tolerance, most often due to desensitization of the drug receptors (e.g. benzodiazepines). Tolerance can also develop from slower adaptive changes like up-regulation of receptors with antagonists and down-regulation with agonists.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true about the action of drugs on receptors?

options.text: An agonist activates a receptor to produce an effect
An inverse agonist activates a receptor to produce an effect in the opposite direction to that of the well recognized agonist
An antagonist prevents the action of an agonist on a receptor or the subsequent response, but does not have any effect of its own
A partial agonist activates a receptor to produce a submaximal effect that antagonizes the action of a full agonist
All of the above

questions.explanation: An agonist is a compound that mimics the action of a neurotransmitter; an antagonist is a compound that blocks or inhibits the action of a neurotransmitter.

questions.question_text: Foods not to be taken with tranylcypromine include all of the following, except:

options.text: Ricotta cheese
Red wine
Pickled herring
Broad bean pods
Fermented soya bean extract

questions.explanation: All cheeses except cream, cottage and ricotta should be avoided.

questions.question_text: Tranylcypromine is contraindicated in all of the following, except:

options.text: Severe hepatic impairment
Epilepsy
Hyperthyroidism
Phaeochromocytoma
Severe cerebrovascular disease

questions.explanation: Tranylcypromine is an MAOI with an amphetamine-like stimulating effect that may be helpful in patients with anergia and retardation.

questions.question_text: Moclobemide:

options.text: Is a reversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase type A
Is licensed for use in social anxiety disorder
Causes less potentiation of pressor effects of tyramine than irreversible MAOIs
Should not be combined with SSRIs, because a serotonin syndrome may result
All of the above

questions.explanation: Moclobemide is the most recently developed MAOI.

questions.question_text: Regarding special properties of drugs belonging to the tricyclic antidepressant class, all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Amoxapine produces significant blockade of dopamine D 2receptors
Clomipramine is the most potent 5-HT reuptake inhibitor in the class
Lofepramine is a sedating antidepressant
Use of maprotiline in higher doses has been associated with a higher incidence of seizures
Desipramine causes insomnia

questions.explanation: TCAs inhibit the reuptake of both 5-HT and noradrenaline.

questions.question_text: Recognized side-effects of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) include all of the following, except:

options.text: Worsening of glaucoma
Urinary incontinence
Heart block
Cognitive impairment
Sexual dysfunction

questions.explanation: TCAs cause retention of urine.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), except:

options.text: They are primarily eliminated by hepatic metabolism
Fluoxetine has the longest half-life in the class
They inhibit CYP450 enzymes, resulting in potential interactions with other drugs
Withdrawal reaction occurs more commonly with a longer half-life
The gastrointestinal side-effects are usually dose related

correct_answer.text: Withdrawal reaction occurs more commonly with a longer half-life

correct_answers.text: Withdrawal reaction occurs more commonly with a longer half-life

questions.explanation: Paroxetine has the shortest half-life.

questions.question_text: All of the following side-effects are usually associated with SSRIs, except:

options.text: Weight gain
Extra-pyramidal side-effects
Ejaculatory delay and anorgasmia
Hyponatraemia secondary to syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone (SIADH)
Increased risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding

questions.explanation: Weight gain is a side-effect of lithium.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about SSRIs, except:

options.text: They are recommended in combination therapy with MAOIs in resistant depression
They may cause myoclonus and seizures when used with lithium and tryptophan
They may potentiate the induction of extra-pyramidal movement disorders by antipsychotic drugs
Serotonin toxicity may occur if combined with sumatryptan
They may increase the plasma levels of risperidone

correct_answer.text: They are recommended in combination therapy with MAOIs in resistant depression

correct_answers.text: They are recommended in combination therapy with MAOIs in resistant depression

questions.explanation: Simultaneous administration of SSRIs and MAOIs causes 5-HT toxicity syndrome (the serotonin syndrome) with agitation, hyperpyrexia, rigidity, myoclonus, coma and death. Other drugs (lithium, tryptophan, 5-HT receptor agonist sumatryptan) that increase brain 5-HT function also cause similar reactions.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Priapism is a serious side-effect of trazodone
Nefazodone elevates the plasma levels of haloperidol
Reboxetine is a reversible inhibitor of MAO-A
Mainserin can cause fatal agranulocytosis
L-tryptophan is associated with eosinophilia–myalgia syndrome

correct_answer.text: Reboxetine is a reversible inhibitor of MAO-A

correct_answers.text: Reboxetine is a reversible inhibitor of MAO-A

questions.explanation: Reboxetine is a selective noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor.

questions.question_text: Venlafaxine:

options.text: Is a noradrenaline and serotonin specific antidepressant (NASSA)
Is recommended for combined use with moclobemide in resistant depression
May cause postural hypotension and dose-related hypertension
Is more toxic in overdose than tricyclic antidepressants
May cause high plasma sodium levels

correct_answer.text: May cause postural hypotension and dose-related hypertension

correct_answers.text: May cause postural hypotension and dose-related hypertension

questions.explanation: Venlafaxine is a selective serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor (SNRI). Combination with moclobemide causes serotonin syndrome. Preliminary evidence suggests that it is less toxic in overdose than tricyclic antidepressants.

questions.question_text: L-tryptophan:

options.text: Has direct action on 5-HT receptors
Has a low protein binding
Can enhance the antidepressant effects of MAOIs
Is non-sedative
High doses are associated with decrease in slow-wave sleep

correct_answer.text: Can enhance the antidepressant effects of MAOIs

correct_answers.text: Can enhance the antidepressant effects of MAOIs

questions.explanation: L-tryptophan is a precursor of 5-HT. It is highly protein binding. It can cause serotonin syndrome with SSRIs and MAOIs. It is a sedative. High doses are associated with an increase in slow-wave sleep.

questions.question_text: All of the following properties of SSRIs are thought to be mediated mainly by the subtypes of 5-HT receptors, except:

options.text: 5-HT 1receptor: antidepressant action
5-HT 2receptor: anxiolytic action
5-HT 2receptor: sexual dysfunction
5-HT 3receptor: nausea
5-HT 3receptor: headache

questions.explanation: 5-HT 1receptor, anxiolytic; 5-HT 2receptor, insomnia, agitation and sexual dysfunction.

questions.question_text: St John's wort:

options.text: Increases the anticoagulant effect of warfarin
Reduces the plasma concentration of amitriptyline
Reduces the serotoninergic effects of SSRIs
Increases plasma concentration of aripiprazole
Increases plasma concentration of digoxin

correct_answer.text: Reduces the plasma concentration of amitriptyline

correct_answers.text: Reduces the plasma concentration of amitriptyline

questions.explanation: St John's wort reduces the anticoagulant effect of warfarin, increases the serotoninergic effects of SSRIs, reduces the plasma concentration of aripiprazole, digoxin, simvastatin, theophylline, carbamazepine and phenytoin, and reduces the contraceptive effects of oestrogen and progesterone.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about lithium, except:

options.text: It is the smallest alkaline cation
It acts through second messengers
It is not metabolized in the body
It is highly protein bound
It is reabsorbed in the proximal tubule

questions.explanation: Lithium is not bound to proteins.

questions.question_text: In relation to lithium:

options.text: Lithium is transported in the proximal tubule in competition with sodium
When the proximal tubule absorbs more water, lithium absorption decreases
Dehydration causes plasma lithium concentration to fall
Hyponatraemia causes plasma lithium concentration to fall
Thiazide diuretics cause plasma lithium concentration to fall

correct_answer.text: Lithium is transported in the proximal tubule in competition with sodium

correct_answers.text: Lithium is transported in the proximal tubule in competition with sodium

questions.explanation: When the proximal tubule absorbs more water, lithium absorption decreases; dehydration, hyponatraemia and thiazide diuretics cause plasma lithium concentration to fall.

questions.question_text: All of the following are adverse renal effects of lithium, except:

options.text: Nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
Minimal change glomerulonephritis
Renal cell carcinoma
Reduced glomerular filtration rate (GFR) and renal failure
Interstitial nephritis

questions.explanation: Lithium blocks the effects of ADH on the renal tubule.

questions.question_text: Excretion of lithium is reduced by all of the following, except:

options.text: ACE inhibitors
Indomethacin
Acetazolamide
Furosemide
Amiloride

questions.explanation: Insufficient intake of water in patients with lithium-induced polyuria may lead to a rapid lowering of lithium clearance and, hence, to a rise in the serum lithium concentration and development of intoxication.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about lithium, except:

options.text: There is an increased risk of hypothyroidism when lithium is given with amiodarone
Carbamazepine increases plasma concentration of lithium and causes neurotoxicity
There is an increased risk of extra-pyramidal side-effects and neuro-toxicity when lithium is given with antipsychotics
There is an increased risk of extra-pyramidal side-effects when lithium is given with metoclopramide
Antacids and theophylline cause increased excretion of lithium

correct_answer.text: Carbamazepine increases plasma concentration of lithium and causes neurotoxicity

correct_answers.text: Carbamazepine increases plasma concentration of lithium and causes neurotoxicity

questions.explanation: Carbamazepine when given with lithium causes neurotoxicity without increasing the plasma concentration of lithium.

questions.question_text: All of the following are recognized side-effects of lithium, except:

options.text: Weight loss
Hair loss
Hypothyroidism
Hyperparathyroidism
Osteoporosis

questions.explanation: Weight gain is a side-effect of lithium.

questions.question_text: The effects of lithium on thyroid include:

options.text: Interference with iodine uptake
Interference with tyrosine iodination
Interference with release of T3 and T4
Increased levels of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)
All of the above

questions.explanation: Thyroid enlargement occurs in 5% and hypothyroidism in 20% of women treated with lithium.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true, except:

options.text: Lithium treatment may cause remission of pre-existing psoriasis
The thyroid dysfunction as a result of lithium treatment occurs more commonly in women
Weight gain as a result of lithium treatment occurs more commonly in women
Osteoporosis as a result of lithium treatment occurs more commonly in women
Propanol may reduce tremor associated with lithium treatment

correct_answer.text: Lithium treatment may cause remission of pre-existing psoriasis

correct_answers.text: Lithium treatment may cause remission of pre-existing psoriasis

questions.explanation: Lithium treatment may cause exacerbation of pre-existing psoriasis.

questions.question_text: Regarding treatment with lithium in pregnancy:

options.text: The absolute risk of the cardiac malformation Ebstein's anomaly is very high
The period of maximum risk is second trimester
Neonatal goitre can occur
At parturition, diuresis may lead to reduced serum levels of lithium
Lithium is safe in breastfeeding

questions.explanation: The absolute risk of Ebstein's anomaly (right ventricular hypoplasia and tricuspid valve insufficiency) is low at 1:1000, but the relative risk is 10–20 times higher than control. The period of maximum risk is the first trimester (2–6 weeks). Neonatal goitre, hypotonia and arrhythmias can occur. Parturition diuresis may lead to increased serum levels of lithium, leading to toxicity because of the reduced plasma volume and redistribution.

questions.question_text: In lithium toxicity all of the following are true, except:

options.text: Early clinical signs may include apathy
Constipation is a usual sign
Convulsions and coma occur
Concentrations above 2mmol/litre are usually associated with serious toxicity
Haemodialysis may be needed

questions.explanation: Diarrhoea, vomiting, tremor, etc. are the usual signs of lithium toxicity.

questions.question_text: The pharmacodynamic properties of carbamazepine include:

options.text: Binding to voltage-dependent sodium channels and prolonging their inactivation
Reducing voltage-dependent calcium channel activation and therefore synaptic transmission
Reduction of current through NMDA receptor channels
Competitive antagonism of adenosine A 1receptors
All of the above

questions.explanation: Carbamazepine is effective as an antiepileptic, as prophylaxis of bipolar disorder, and in management of acute mania.

questions.question_text: Significant pharmacodynamic interaction occurs between carbamazepine and:

options.text: Antipsychotics
TCAs
Calcium channel blockers
Lithium
All of the above

questions.explanation: Carbamazepine is a strong inducer of hepatic microsomal enzymes.

questions.question_text: Carbamazepine:

options.text: Commonly causes agranulocytosis
Is safe in disturbances in cardiac conduction
Usually causes clinical hypothyroidism
Is associated with high sodium states
Induces its own metabolism

questions.explanation: Agranulocytosis is a serious but rare side-effect; carbamazepine is contraindicated in cardiac conduction abnormalities, lowers plasma thyroxine concentration (though clinical hypothyroidism is unusual) and is associated with low sodium states.

questions.question_text: In bipolar illness, which of the following is a predictor of good response to treatment with lithium?

options.text: Family history of bipolar illness
Prominent depressive features
Psychotic symptoms
Rapid cycling
None of the above

questions.explanation: b, c and d are indicators of poor response.

questions.question_text: Valproate:

options.text: Induces hepatic microsomal enzymes
Has many active metabolites
Is not useful in longer-term prophylaxis of bipolar disorder
Is a drug of choice in generalized absences and myoclonic epilepsy
Has low protein binding

correct_answer.text: Is a drug of choice in generalized absences and myoclonic epilepsy

correct_answers.text: Is a drug of choice in generalized absences and myoclonic epilepsy

questions.explanation: Unlike carbamazapine, valproate does not induce hepatic microsomal enzymes and, if anything, tends to delay the metabolism of other drugs.

questions.question_text: Valproate:

options.text: Is known to decrease synaptic levels of GABA
Is a preferred choice over lithium in pregnancy
Is not useful in patients with bipolar illness who are unresponsive to lithium and carbamazepine
Is not secreted in breast milk
Is not safe in hepatic dysfunction

correct_answer.text: Is not safe in hepatic dysfunction

correct_answers.text: Is not safe in hepatic dysfunction

questions.explanation: Valproate is 80–95% protein bound; it has no active metabolites; it does not induce hepatic enzymes but delays metabolism of some drugs that are metabolized in the liver; it is hepatotoxic; it increases synaptic levels of GABA and causes major congenital malformations (e.g. spina bifida, neural tube defects in up to 5%); folate reduces the risk. Up to 10% of serum concentration is secreted in breast milk.

questions.question_text: Common side-effects of valproate include:

options.text: Sedation
Fatal hepatic toxicity
Thrombocytopenia
Acute pancreatitis
Amenorrhoea

questions.explanation: The others are less common side-effects.

questions.question_text: Valproate increases the concentration of all of the following, except:

options.text: Erythromycin
Lamotrigine
Phenytoin
Diazepam
Barbiturates

questions.explanation: Valproate reduces the concentration of erythromycin.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about lamotrigine, except:

options.text: It blocks voltage-dependent calcium channels
It reduces the release of excitatory neurotransmitter glutamate
It is effective as a monotherapy in the treatment of bipolar depression
Adverse effects include Stevens–Johnson syndrome
Plasma levels can be lowered by carbamazepine

questions.explanation: Lamotrigine blocks voltage-dependent sodium channels.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about gabapentin, except:

options.text: It is a GABA receptor agonist
It increases GABA turnover in the brain
It has a sedating profile
It has anxiolytic properties
It is excreted entirely by the kidney

correct_answer.text: It is a GABA receptor agonist

correct_answers.text: It is a GABA receptor agonist

questions.explanation: Gabapentin was developed as a structural analogue of GABA but it has no activity on GABA receptors or the GABA transporter.

questions.question_text: Psychostimulants:

options.text: Include methylphenidate and cocaine
Increase the release and block the reuptake of dopamine and noradrenaline
Are used to treat narcolepsy
Are useful in the hyperkinetic syndrome of childhood
All of the above

questions.explanation: Psychostimulants include caffeine, amphetamine, methylphenidate, cocaine, etc.

questions.question_text: Benzodiazepines:

options.text: Increase the affinity of GABA Areceptor for GABA
Are strongly bound to the plasma proteins
Are lipophilic
Agonist effects can be reversed by flumazenil
All of the above

questions.explanation: Benzodiazepines pass readily into the brain.

questions.question_text: Buspirone:

options.text: Is a partial agonist at 5-HT 1Areceptors
Is an agonist at dopamine D 2receptors
Is useful in treating benzodiazepine withdrawal
T olerance and dependence occur commonly
Is highly sedative

questions.explanation: Buspirone is an antagonist at D 2; tolerance and dependence will not occur usually; it is not a sedative but may cause light-headedness.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true about hypnotics?

options.text: Zopiclone produces more changes in sleep architecture than benzodiazepines
Zolpidem acts at benzodiazepine receptors
Zaleplon does not cause a dependence syndrome
Taste disturbance is a rare side-effect of zopiclone
Clomethiazole is safe to use in alcohol-dependent patients who continue to drink

questions.explanation: Zopiclone produces fewer changes in sleep architecture. Taste disturbance is common.

questions.question_text: Flumazenil:

options.text: Is a benzodiazepine antagonist, producing few pharmacological effects by itself
Is available only for intravenous use
Is useful in reversing acute toxicity produced by benzodiazepines
Carries a risk of provoking acute benzodiazepine withdrawal
All of the above

questions.explanation: Flumazenil does not antagonize the central nervous system effects of drugs affecting GABA-ergic neurons other than the benzodiazepine receptor (including ethanol, barbiturates and general anaesthetics) and does not reverse the effects of opioids.

questions.question_text: Regarding benzodiazepines:

options.text: Actions are mediated through specific receptor sites on GABA receptors
Benzodiazepines with high potency and shorter half-lives are more associated with dependence and withdrawal
Benzodiazepines can cause respiratory depression when combined with clozapine
Withdrawal syndrome is associated epileptic seizures
All of the above

questions.explanation: Benzodiazepines are anxiolytic, sedative and hypnotic, muscle relaxant, and anticonvulsant.

questions.question_text: All of the following statements are true about treatment with benzodiazepines, except:

options.text: Dependence is likely in patients with a history of alcohol or drug abuse
Dependence is likely in patients with marked personality disorders
Lorazepam and oxazepam may be preferred in patients with hepatic impairment
They are safe in myasthenia gravis
They may cause paradoxical increase in aggression

correct_answer.text: They are safe in myasthenia gravis

correct_answers.text: They are safe in myasthenia gravis

questions.explanation: Benzodiazepines are contraindicated in myasthenia gravis (increased respiratory depression).

questions.question_text: Safe psychotropic medications in porphyria include:

options.text: Amphetamine
TCAs
MAOIs
Mianserin
Barbiturates

questions.explanation: Drugs that lead to increased activity of the hepatic P450 system, such as phenobarbital, sulfonamides, oestrogens and alcohol, are associated with porphyria.

questions.question_text: All of the following are true about anxiolytics, except:

options.text: Propranolol is effectively used to treat bodily symptoms of anxiety
Meprobamate is less hazardous in overdose than benzodiazepines
Barbiturate withdrawal may be fatal
Benzodiazepines cause amnesia
Buspirone has no affinity for benzodiazepine receptors

correct_answer.text: Meprobamate is less hazardous in overdose than benzodiazepines

correct_answers.text: Meprobamate is less hazardous in overdose than benzodiazepines

questions.explanation: Meprobamate is less effective and more hazardous in overdose than benzodiazepines and can induce dependence.

questions.question_text: Drugs useful in narcolepsy include all of the following, except:

options.text: Dexamphetamine
Methylphenidate
Modafinil
Sibutramine
Tricyclic antidepressants

questions.explanation: Sibutramine is a centrally acting appetite suppressant used in treatment for obesity. TCAs and SSRIs do not affect the sleep disorder but may reduce the frequency of cataplexy.
